# Check catalog

<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @openverify/docs-tools docs:catalog` (packages/docs-tools/src/catalog/); do not edit by hand. -->

Every check (`CHECK_REGISTRY`, 89), report type (`REPORT_REGISTRY`, 11) and signal (`SIGNAL_REGISTRY`, 19) as the registries in `@openverify/core` state them, with the configuration defaults the workers merge, the calibration reports' summary blocks and what each does not detect ([limits.json](limits.json), ours). The catalog says only what those state (C279.4); each family page is the full description.

- **Tier** (ADR 0002): R real, deterministic logic over values; H heuristic; A adapter to a provider. Two letters name a secondary tier. Every H, A/H and H/A check and every model-based one is `beta`.
- **Model**: whether a learned model can decide the check.
- **Configuration (default)**: the keys a template may set; a key with no default applies only when a template sets it.
- **Calibration**: the report and the rows that measure it, each with its figure and verdict. `-`: no report measures it. A cited report with no row: no variant was built to trip it, or the report measures it without a row of its own.
- IP geolocation by [DB-IP](https://db-ip.com) (CC BY 4.0): the network signals and the `ip-address` report read DB-IP Lite.

| `id_nfc_mrz_comparison` | - | R | fraud | ga | upload, history | no | none | - | OCR confusables are tolerated on every reading, since whether the printed check digits held is not recorded; a chip of another issuer finds no reference (no_reference_data), and issuer_mismatch is never answered. |
| `id_nfc_selfie_comparison` | - | R | fraud | beta | upload, vision, history | yes | `threshold` 0.394 | [selfie-phase4.md](../calibration/selfie-phase4.md): `face-match-threshold-far-1e-3` 0.3862, reported; `shared-threshold-far` 0.00, reported<br>[selfie-phase4-method.md](../calibration/selfie-phase4-method.md) | The 0.394 threshold was calibrated on studio portrait pairs, not on chip portraits, and is provisional here. Without a decided selfie it answers no_reference_data: chip data alone does not identify the presenter. |
| `id_nfc_repeat_detection` | - | R | fraud | ga | upload, history | no | `sighting-outcome` review | - | Ours. A chip seen on another account goes to review by default (fail only with sighting-outcome: fail); a match without established integrity answers integrity_not_established. |

## `crypto_wallet`

4 checks. Family page: [crypto-wallet.md](crypto-wallet.md).

| Check | Source API name | Tier | Type | Stage | Inputs | Model | Configuration (default) | Calibration | Does not detect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crypto_wallet_validity_detection` | `crypto_wallet_validity_detection` | R | user_behavior | ga | upload | no | `require-evm-checksum` false | - | It checks the address's format and checksum only. An all-lower-case or all-upper-case EVM address carries no checksum and passes unless require-evm-checksum is set; a valid address may still belong to someone else. |
| `crypto_wallet_disallowed_chain_detection` | `crypto_wallet_disallowed_chain_detection` | R | fraud | ga | upload | no | none | - | Without allowed-chains every offered chain is allowed (no_allowlist, non-blocking). It judges the chain the user claimed, not where funds move. |
| `crypto_wallet_address_comparison` | `crypto_wallet_address_comparison` | R/A | user_behavior | ga | upload, provider | no | `bip137-mode` loose; `allow-high-s` true; `allow-contract-wallets` false | - | One ownership proof per chain family: no transaction-based proof, no proof of funds, no BIP-322 full or multisig scripts (signature_inconclusive). A counterfactual (ERC-6492) EVM wallet is inconclusive. Ownership is proven at signing time only; nothing watches the address afterwards. |
| `crypto_wallet_statement_comparison` | `crypto_wallet_statement_comparison` | R | fraud | ga | upload | no | none | - | It passes only for a signature the address check verified over exactly the challenge's bytes; it says nothing about later use of the key. |

## `database_business`

5 checks. Family page: [business.md](business.md).

| Check | Source API name | Tier | Type | Stage | Inputs | Model | Configuration (default) | Calibration | Does not detect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `database_business_identity_comparison` | `database_business_identity_comparison` | R/A | fraud | ga | upload, provider | no | `match-groups` {name: partial, registration-number: full} or {name: partial, address: partial} | - | GLEIF misses most small businesses, and sole traders and partnerships are on no company register: both go to review, never to a failure. EDGAR is searched by name among listed companies only. |
| `database_business_active_business_detection` | `database_business_active_business_detection` | R/A | fraud | ga | upload, provider | no | `fail-on-lapsed-lei` false | - | GLEIF lists only businesses with an LEI, and EDGAR has no status, so many businesses go to review (status_not_available or no_registry_record), never to a failure. Source answer shapes for Companies House and EDGAR were not checked against the live services. |
| `database_business_associated_persons_comparison` | `database_business_associated_persons_comparison` | R/A | fraud | ga | upload, provider | no | `min-match-level` partial | - | Only the first 100 officers and persons with significant control of a Companies House record are read; a source that lists no persons answers source_has_no_persons. |
| `database_business_enabled_country_detection` | `database_business_enabled_country_detection` | R | user_behavior | ga | upload | no | none | - | Without the type's allowed-countries it answers no_allowlist and never blocks. |
| `database_business_service_available_detection` | `database_business_service_available_detection` | R | user_behavior | ga | upload, provider | no | none | - | It reports only whether a bound register covering the country answered; outside every bound register's countries it answers provider_not_configured. |

4 checks. Family page: [business.md](business.md).

| Check | Source API name | Tier | Type | Stage | Inputs | Model | Configuration (default) | Calibration | Does not detect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `business_website_resolution_detection` | - | R | user_behavior | ga | upload, provider | no | none | - | Ours. It shows only that the domain resolves to a public address, not that the business operates the site. |
| `business_website_domain_age_detection` | `business_website_domain_age_detection` | R | fraud | ga | upload, provider | no | `min-domain-age-days` 90 | - | RDAP does not cover every TLD and never a subdomain on a platform: both answer domain_age_unavailable. ## Lists, the graph and transactions

The `custom-list` report and the completion screening read lists; the graph and transactions are not report types and run no check, so they are listed here for their kinds and caps only.

### Lists

13 kinds (`LIST_KIND_REGISTRY`). The match method of each kind is in [the lists page](../lists/README.md#kinds).

| Kind | Item id prefix | CSV importer | Biometric | Screened by `screen: all` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `browser-fingerprint` | `libf` | yes | no | yes |
| `device-fingerprint` | `lidf` | yes | no | yes |
| `country` | `lic` | yes | no | yes |
| `email-address` | `liea` | yes | no | yes |
| `face` | `lifc` | no | yes | no |
| `geolocation` | `ligl` | yes | no | yes |
| `government-id-number` | `ligin` | yes | no | yes |
| `field` | `liif` | yes | no | yes |
| `ip-address` | `liip` | yes | no | yes |
| `name` | `lin` | yes | no | yes |
| `phone-number` | `lipn` | yes | no | yes |
| `selfie-background` | `lisb` | no | yes | no |
| `string` | `lis` | yes | no | no |

- Match methods (`LIST_MATCH_METHODS`): `exact`, `cidr`, `radius`, `fuzzy_name`, `face_cosine`, `background`.
- A list that could not be read is `unscreened` with one of (`LIST_UNSCREENED_REASONS`): `list_items_pending`, `probe_unavailable`, `probe_too_coarse`, `consent_not_given`, `normaliser_outdated`, `key_rotated`, `limit_exceeded`, `list_archived`, `method_not_on_demand`, `kind_not_collected`, `client_address_untrusted`; never "no match".
- A list the subject has no value for is `not-applicable` with: `subject_has_no_value`.
- Caps (`LIST_LIMITS`): `activeListsPerEnvironment` 1000, `itemsPerList` 1000000, `itemsPerBiometricList` 10000, `radiusMeters` 500000, `nameLength` 255, `stringValueLength` 255, `itemRetentionDays` 3650, `dismissReasonLength` 500, `matchProbes` 20, `screenedLists` 50, `reportLists` 20.
- Method constants (`LIST_MATCH_CONSTANTS`): `fuzzy-name-candidate-cap` 5000 (calibrated), `face-list-threshold` 0.72 (calibrated), `background-candidates` 5 (provisional), `biometric-cache-bytes` 67108864 (provisional), `biometric-cache-idle-minutes` 10 (provisional).

| Signal | Public | Tier | Stage | Layer | Collection | Inputs | Decisive alone | Does not detect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inquiry/bot_score` | yes | H | beta | behaviour | session-integrity | integrity, android-integrity, behaviour, request-headers | yes | Real-device or OS-level automation, patched browsers and fraud-farm humans; a low score proves nothing. |
| `inquiry/behavior_threat_level` | yes | H | beta | behaviour | session-integrity | integrity, behaviour | yes | Needs at least 3 screens and 20 input events, otherwise null (insufficient_behaviour). |
| `inquiry/automation_artefact_count` | no | R | ga | device | session-integrity | integrity, android-integrity | yes | The data is reported by the client; 0 carries no_artefact_found, not 'human'. |
| `inquiry/session_count` | no | R | ga | ensemble | server | sessions | yes | A server-API inquiry has no flow sessions. |
| `inquiry/network_threat_level` | no | H | beta | network | server | network | yes | Residential proxies and most VPNs; low means 'no listed risk found'. |
| `inquiry/tor_detected` | no | R | ga | network | server | network, tor-exit-addresses | yes | IPv6 (the exit list has no IPv6 exits); false only when every session was a public IPv4 address checked against a fresh list. |
| `inquiry/datacenter_detected` | no | R | ga | network | server | network, cloud-ranges | yes | Anything outside the providers' published ranges; never false. |
| `inquiry/vpn_detected` | no | H | beta | network | server | network, asn-seeds | yes | Most VPNs (they rent general hosting); never false. |
| `inquiry/proxy_detected` | no | A | beta | network | server | network, ipReputation | yes | Anything without an ipReputation adapter bound. |
| `inquiry/country_from_session` | yes | H | beta | network | server | network, dbip-country-lite | yes | VPNs, roaming and corporate egress; an IP country is approximate (IP geolocation by DB-IP). |
| `inquiry/country_comparison` | yes | H | beta | ensemble | server | network, dbip-country-lite, government-id-extraction | yes | Null for Tor, VPN-ASN, provider-range or privacy-relay sessions (ip_country_unreliable); an IP country is approximate (IP geolocation by DB-IP). |
| `inquiry/max_session_distance` | no | R | ga | network | server | network, dbip-city-lite | yes | Needs DB-IP City Lite (off by default); a country is not a point, and a city point is a coarse estimate. |
| `inquiry/handoff_count` | no | R | ga | handoff | server | sessions, handoffs | yes | It counts device handoffs only; it says nothing about who used each device. |
| `inquiry/device_emulated` | no | H | beta | device | session-integrity | android-integrity | no | Emulators that hide their build properties; never false. Not decisive alone. |
| `inquiry/device_rooted` | no | H | beta | device | session-integrity | android-integrity | no | Root hiding (Magisk's DenyList, Zygisk modules); never false or 'not rooted'. Not decisive alone. |
| `inquiry/device_hooked` | no | H | beta | device | session-integrity | android-integrity | no | Renamed or late-injected hooking tools; never false. Not decisive alone. |
| `inquiry/device_integrity_level` | no | A | beta | device | session-integrity | integrity-verdict | no | The person; camera injection or a relay on a certified device; devices without Google Play. Not decisive alone. |
| `inquiry/app_recognized` | no | A | beta | device | session-integrity | integrity-verdict | no | A sideloaded or self-built host app is unrecognized by design; UNEVALUATED is null, never false. Not decisive alone. |
| `inquiry/list_match_count` | no | R | ga | list | server | lists | yes | It counts open list matches only; a list that could not be read is listed as unscreened, never counted as no match. Never a review rule. |
